newsitem.title: FRANCE: France denies delay tactics on Nazi gold.
newsitem.headline: France denies delay tactics on Nazi gold.

text.p: France denied on Thursday it was stalling on a request from the World Jewish Congress (WJC) for restitution of Nazi gold seized from Jews and now jointly held by France, Britain and the United States.
"We have indeed received a letter about this from the World Jewish Congress which will be examined and replied to as soon as possible," foreign ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said.
"It is therefore entirely wrong to say our attitude on this subject is different from that of the U.S. or Britain," he told reporters.

He was replying to questions about an interview published on Thursday by the newspaper Le Figaro with WJC executive director Elan Steinberg. Steinberg said Paris had adopted delaying tactics over the gold.
Steinberg said the three wartime allies held seven tonnes of Nazi gold seized from Holocaust victims which the WJC said should be given to descendants.

"The U.S. and Britain are in favour of the move but France has replied with delaying tactics which is regrettable," Steinberg said. Jewish groups are also seeking to trace assets seized by the Nazis and transferred to Swiss banks.
